papers.title: The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models
papers.abstract: Deep learning algorithms have become widely used and successful across a wide range of tasks. A key challenge is determining whether these algorithms truly capture the intrinsic geometry of their training data in order to better understand what they learn from data. In this theoretical work, we explore a new geometric structure defined on the data space by a trained neural network through the Data Information Matrix (DIM), a variation of the Fisher Information Matrix. This new geometric structure is a foliation and the main focus of this work is to explore the non-smooth case of ReLU activation functions, where traditional geometric tools often fail. The foliation is defined through a distribution spanned by the columns of the DIM. We first prove that this distribution is non-smooth in the sense of distributions, rendering the existence of an associated foliation much more complex. To circumvent this issue, we introduce a smoothed version of this distribution that differs from the original only on a set of measure zero. Finally, we prove that this smoothed distribution induces a singular foliation on the data space, which is based on the data the network has been trained with. Our theoretical contributions provide a geometric framework to better understand how neural networks organize their input space in non-smooth settings, bridging differential geometry and deep learning theory.

papers.title: Klt varieties with semipositive anticanonical bundle : symmetric tensors, holonomy and structure
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to study klt projective varieties such that the anticanonical bundle is semipositive from the differential-geometric point of view. The study of the holonomy of such varieties yields generalizations of several results. We show that the dimension of the space of symmetric differentials is bounded by a constant depending on the augmented irregularity, generalizing a result of Kobayashi. If we endow such a variety $X$ with a metric $\omega$ whose Ricci curvature is non-negative, then we show that the holonomy of the regular locus is compact. If we assume that $X$ has canonical singularities, then we show that the general fiber of the Albanese map can be decomposed into a product of irreducible Calabi-Yau varieties, irreducible holomorphic symplectic varieties and hereditarily rationally connected varieties by the holonomy generalizing a structure theorem of Campana, Demailly and Peternell. To conclude, we show that the fundamental group of the regular locus of such varieties is virtually abelian.

papers.title: Bubble Tree Convergence for Minimisers of a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
papers.abstract: We study degree $1$ minimisers $u: (\Sigma,g) \to S^2$ for a Baby-Skyrme model with a Sacks-Uhlenbeck regularisation term $E^{\alpha}(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_{\Sigma} (1+\vert \nabla u \vert^2)^{\alpha+1} -1 dv_g$ and establish convergence of degree $1$ minimisers to a simple bubble tree as $\alpha \to 0$. We also obtain a new no-neck result for the classical Sacks-Uhlenbeck energy $E^{\alpha}$.

papers.title: Boundary Plateau Laws I
papers.abstract: We give a complete list of the possible local shapes of soap films where they wet the whole wire. In rigorous terms, given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we study $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$.

papers.title: Boundary Plateau Laws II
papers.abstract: Given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we classify $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$. The main idea of this paper is due to an LLM, and the paper was written by an LLM, under the guidance of the authors.

papers.title: $L^p$ Convergence of AMV Laplacians on completions of Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study conditions for the $L^p$ convergence of the AMV Laplacian $\Delta_r$ on completions of Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$. The condition invloves the Minkowski dimension of the set $\overline{M} \setminus M$ and how much the curvature is blowing up around $S$. We build a concrete family of sets that satisfies these conditions, and provide an example of non convergence when these conditions are not met.

papers.title: The inverse Monge--Amp\`ere flow on klt Fano varieties
papers.abstract: We establish the long time existence of the inverse Monge--Amp\`ere flow on a klt $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano variety $X$. We further prove that $X$ admits a K\"ahler--Einstein metric if and only if the flow converges in $L^1$.

papers.title: The Costa surface with a free-boundary hole: an embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with three ends
papers.abstract: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface outside the unit ball whose compact boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. By Mazet and Mendes, in $\mathbb{R}^3$ every such surface with one regular end is a catenoidal piece, and every stable one with parallel embedded regular ends is catenoidal. We construct connected embedded examples with three ends from the Costa surface $M$, placed so that its central saddle point is at the origin. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ we perturb $\varepsilon^{-1}(M\setminus B_\varepsilon)$ into a properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface of genus one with one boundary circle and three ends, two catenoidal and one planar. The construction is a small-hole perturbation. The only error of the initial surface is in the boundary condition. The symmetry group of the Costa surface removes all obstructions: at the hole it forbids the logarithmic and the tilting modes, and globally it kills the bounded Jacobi fields of the Costa surface, which is nondegenerate by Nayatani. In the conformal compactification the Jacobi operator is smooth also at the ends, so the linear analysis takes place on a compact torus with one small hole. The same construction applied to the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces gives such examples of every genus $k\geq1$, of index at least $2k+3$. We also report numerical experiments with two independent implementations of the Costa surface. They confirm the period condition, the symmetries, the boundary error, the index and nullity of the Jacobi operator and the absence of an equivariant kernel. They also compute the free-boundary correction near the hole, which gives pictures of the surfaces.

papers.title: Localization of weighted Goldman volume on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\R)$-Hitchin Component
papers.abstract: We compute Goldman volume on the moduli space of convex real projective structures on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two, with exponential weight defined by the shifted Blaschke area. For every positive parameter, the integral converges and is a finite sum of inverse powers of that parameter. Its coefficients are intersection numbers involving the bundle of regular cubic differentials on the moduli stack of stable curves. The proof establishes absolute convergence and vanishing signed boundary integrals of the transgression under simultaneous plumbing degeneration. The pushforward of Goldman measure by the shifted Blaschke area therefore has a polynomial density on $[0,\infty)$, and its sublevel volumes are polynomial in the threshold.

papers.title: A periodic minimal hypersurface in Euclidean 4-space with Clifford cone singularities
papers.abstract: Let $\sigma(t)=\operatorname{sl}(\varpi t)$ be the lemniscatic sine, normalized to have period $2$. We study the zero set $\mathscr{M}$ of $S(x)=\sigma(x_1)\sigma(x_3)-\sigma(x_2)\sigma(x_4)$ in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$. We show that $\mathscr{M}$ is a complete embedded minimal hypersurface with infinitely many isolated singularities, which are exactly the vertices of the regular honeycomb of $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ by $24$-cells. Near every singular point $\mathscr{M}$ is an analytic image of the Clifford cone, and $\mathscr{M}$ is a stationary integral varifold with density $\pi/2$ at each singularity. The isometry group of $\mathscr{M}$ is generated by the translations of the root lattice $D_4$ and a hyperoctahedral group of order $384$ fixing the centre of a $24$-cell; it has index three in the symmetry group of the honeycomb, acts transitively on the singular points, and contains a symmetry which is not visible from the defining equation. Seen from the centre of a $24$-cell, $\mathscr{M}$ is the zero set of a theta series of a translate of the Hurwitz quaternions, which makes the whole symmetry group manifest; the sections of $\mathscr{M}$ by a family of parallel hyperplanes are triply periodic surfaces with cubic symmetry which change topology through conical points. Finally, $\mathscr{M}$ is obtained from a union of $2$-planes by attaching cones over $2$-tori, and its quotient by the lattice of periods is a compact minimal hypersurface in a flat $4$-torus with exactly three singular points and infinite Morse index; we show that its regular part is one-sided and compute its Euler characteristic and integral homology.

papers.title: Silent Orbits and Cancellations in the Wave Trace
papers.abstract: This paper shows that the wave trace of a bounded and strictly convex planar domain may be arbitrarily smooth in a neighborhood of some point in the length spectrum. In other words, the Poisson relation, which asserts that the singular support of the wave trace is contained in the closure of $\pm$ the length spectrum, can almost be made into a strict inclusion. To do so, we construct large families of domains for which there exist multiple periodic billiard orbits having the same length but different Maslov indices. Using the microlocal Balian-Bloch-Zelditch parametrix for wave invariants developed in our previous paper, we solve a large system of equations for the boundary curvature jets, which leads to the required cancellations. We call such periodic orbits silent, since they are undetectable from the ostensibly audible wave trace. Such cancellations show that there are potential limitations in using the wave trace for inverse spectral problems and, more fundamentally, that the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum are inherently different mathematical objects, at least insofar as the wave trace is concerned.

papers.title: A Li-Yau gradient estimate for the Finslerian logarithmic Schr\"{o}dinger equation
papers.abstract: We establish a local Li--Yau type gradient estimate for a nonlinear parabolic equation with logarithmic reaction on a forward complete Finsler metric measure manifold. The coefficients may depend on both space and time. The estimate uses a weighted Ricci curvature lower bound and explicit cutoff bounds for the divergence-form linearized Laplacian. We explain the role of this localization assumption when the reference direction varies with the solution. Applications include a local Harnack inequality for the equation with a potential and an upper bound for positive stationary solutions under a suitable cutoff exhaustion. An appendix gives a variational existence proof for positive bounded initial data, with quantitative bounds on every finite time interval, which is new as far as the authors know.

papers.title: On the distribution kernels of Toeplitz operators on CR manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the distribution kernel of a Toeplitz operator associated with a classical pseudodifferential operator on a compact, embeddable, strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold. The main result consists of a formula for the values at the diagonal of the second coefficient in the expansion of the symbol of the kernel. We also establish asymptotic expansions for Toeplitz operators on the positive part of a compact not necessary strictly pseudoconvex CR orbifold under certain natural assumptions.

papers.title: Quantitative stability and strict inequalities for the Escobar functional
papers.abstract: For Euclidean domains whose boundaries are sufficiently close to a sphere in $C^2$, we bound the deficit of the Escobar constant from below by the squared $H^{3/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, after fixing its constant and first spherical harmonics. This holds in every dimension $n\ge3$ and implies a bound in Fraenkel asymmetry with optimal quadratic power. Under fixed $C^{6,\alpha}$ and size bounds, the asymmetry estimate also holds for star-shaped domains in dimensions $n\ge6$. For compact Riemannian manifolds with minimal boundary and uniform geometric bounds, we prove $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4/\log(\Lambda/a)$ in dimension six and $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4$ in higher dimensions, where $a=\|\mathring{\mathrm{II}}\|_{L^\infty}>0$. A family satisfying the same bounds has deficit comparable to $a^{8/3}$, excluding uniform lower bounds with smaller powers. We also compute the cubic coefficient of the standard boundary bubble quotient and give uniform remainder estimates.

papers.title: Minimal submanifolds confined in space
papers.abstract: Already in $\mathbb{R}^4$, there are many minimal hypersurfaces but few structural results. The half-space theorem fails there: higher-dimensional catenoids are among the many examples contained in a slab. Nevertheless, we show that in any dimension and codimension, the height of a minimal submanifold controls its volume growth: confinement to a narrow cone forces polynomial growth, and sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, the slowest possible. Thus volume bounds, which regularity theory assumes, follow from height alone. The key is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: if an $n$-dimensional stationary integral varifold lies in a thin slab at a given scale, then its volume doubling ratio at that scale is bounded by a universal constant. Iterating this gives the polynomial growth bounds above. Sublinear height is exactly the borderline for Euclidean growth: examples grow at least like $r^{n+4\epsilon^2/5}$ in cones of aperture $\epsilon$. From Euclidean volume growth, we obtain an optimal Bernstein theorem, in all dimensions, for stable minimal hypersurfaces with sublinear height growth, generalizing results of Moser, Bombieri--De Giorgi--Miranda, Trudinger, Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck, and Ecker--Huisken.

papers.title: A dichotomy for minimal submanifolds
papers.abstract: We survey a circle of recent results showing that a minimal submanifold obeys a dichotomy: either it fills up space, spreading out like a space-filling curve, or it is confined, and confinement forces quantitative restrictions. On the confined side these restrictions are both geometric and function-theoretic: Euclidean volume growth, an optimal rate of convergence of the density, complex-curve rigidity for stable surfaces in $\bf{R}^4$, and a Liouville theorem forcing slowly growing harmonic functions on minimal disks to be constant. A prototypical restriction is Euclidean volume growth, which in these results is forced by the geometry rather than assumed. The mechanism is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: a stationary integral varifold trapped in a thin slab at a given scale cannot double its volume by more than a universal factor. We explain how this principle, and the height-excess bounds behind it, produce Euclidean volume growth for submanifolds of sublinearly growing height in every dimension and codimension, the optimal density rate in a slab, the complex-curve and Liouville rigidity above, a higher-codimension Bernstein theorem for disks, one-sided volume bounds, and an optimal stable Bernstein theorem in all dimensions generalizing Moser, Bombieri-De Giorgi-Miranda, Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck and Ecker-Huisken. We describe three regimes with sharp borderlines. In narrow cones the volume grows polynomially with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and the order $\varepsilon^2$ is attained; in wide cones the growth can be arbitrarily fast. For holomorphic curves in $\mathbb{C}^2$, there are also three regimes and the borderline is determined by the K\"ahler angle.

papers.title: Blaschke Conjecture and Complex Geometry
papers.abstract: We provide a complex-geometric approach to the Blaschke conjecture, i.e., that a manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is isometric to a compact rank-one symmetric space (CROSS). In particular, we introduce the great quadric fibration, a complex analogue of the great sphere fibration. Requiring its total space to be a complex submanifold simultaneously explains many properties that a Blaschke manifold is expected to possess, including its Clifford structure, Hopf fibration, and diffeomorphism class. Furthermore, the great quadric bundle coincides with the variety of minimal rational tangents (VMRT) of the ambient Fano variety in the standard CROSS cases, and we explain this through a bend-and-break argument in the setting of the Blaschke conjecture under a suitable complexification assumption. Combining this with Hwang-Mok VMRT recognition, we prove the Blaschke conjecture for manifolds admitting an adapted complex structure on their entire tangent bundles.

papers.title: Topology, Morse Index, and Area of Minimal Surfaces in Three-Manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every closed Riemannian three-manifold $(M^3,\bar g)$, there exists a constant $C=C(M,\bar g)>0$ such that every closed smoothly embedded minimal surface $\Sigma\subset M$ satisfies $b_1(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z}_2)\le C\bigl(\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma)+\operatorname{Area}(\Sigma)\bigr)$, establishing Song's additive genus-index-area conjecture. For closed connected orientable two-sided minimal immersions, we prove the universal inequality $\gamma(\Sigma)\le8\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma)$ in positive Ricci curvature and the estimate $\gamma(\Sigma)\le C(M,\bar g)\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma)$ in positive scalar curvature. In the latter case, we also bound both area and total curvature by $C(M,\bar g)(1+\operatorname{Ind}(\Sigma))$.

papers.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
papers.abstract: We construct closed mean curvature flows with arbitrarily large genus increase in every smooth Riemannian three-manifold, giving counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander in the tangent space at the singular point, smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean curvature flows with prescribed tangent flows (arXiv:2405.15577, arXiv:2607.23879) and the noncompact counterexample (arXiv:2605.09657) gives the desired examples.

papers.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ denote the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces with $n$ cusps. Mirzakhani and Zograf obtained a complete asymptotic expansion as $g\to\infty$ for fixed $n$; its terms are effectively powers of $n^2/g$, so it degenerates once $n$ is of order $\sqrt g$. We prove an asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the genus that is uniform in all $n\ge0$. The leading term is an explicit saddle-point expression whose saddle moves with the cusp density $n/g$. It has relative error $O(g^{-1})$, and truncation at an order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$. For fixed $n$, the leading term confirms Zograf's conjecture that the constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics is $1/\sqrt\pi$. We also determine the asymptotic profiles of volume ratios, uniformly in the number of cusps, and of adjacent coefficients of the one-boundary volume polynomial, uniformly in the degree; this answers two questions of Mirzakhani. The proof uses a positive recursion for mixed $\kappa_1$--$\psi$ intersection numbers, normalized at the pure-$\psi$ endpoint, and a local limit theorem in the number of cusps.

papers.title: Formal Neighborhood Equivariant Cohomology and Kirwan Surjectivity at Singular Values
papers.abstract: Let \(G\) be a compact Lie group acting Hamiltonianly on a symplectic manifold \(M\) with moment map \(\mu:M\to\g^*\). For a singular value \(a\) of \(\mu\), the symplectic quotient \(\mu^{-1}(a)/G\) is stratified and the classical Kirwan map is not defined. We introduce a \emph{formal neighborhood equivariant cohomology} \(\cH_G^*(a)\) using the slice-groupoid Cartan sheaf and the closed embedding \(\mu^{-1}(a)/G\hookrightarrow \mu^{-1}(U_a)/G\) for a \(G\)-invariant neighborhood \(U_a\) of \(a\). We define a formal Kirwan map \[ \kappa_{\mathrm{formal}}:H_G^*(M)\longrightarrow \cH_G^*(a). \] We prove that \(\kappa_{\mathrm{formal}}\) is surjective under a local \emph{equivariant homotopy retraction} condition on the slice level sets \[ C_x=\mu_x^{-1}(a|_{\g_x})\subset S_x, \] which is satisfied, for example, when \(a\) is a regular value of every slice moment map, or when \(a=0\) and \(C_x\) is a \(G_x\)-equivariant cone. The weakest condition we identify is the existence, for each \(x\in\mu^{-1}(a)\), of a local quasi-isomorphism \[ \Car(S_x,G_x)\simeq \cC^\bullet_{C_x} \] in a \(G_x\)-equivariant neighborhood of the orbit, without requiring a global tubular neighborhood. As an application we recover, in the formal framework, the even-degree surjectivity theorem of Delarue--Ramacher--Schmitt for \(S^1\)-actions and clarify why odd-degree surjectivity fails in general.

papers.title: Rigidity and Affine Deformations of Foliations on Nilpotent and Solvable Contact Lie Algebras
papers.abstract: Let g be a Lie algebra of dimension 2n+1, let beta be a contact form, and let alpha be a nonzero integrable 1-form. We study when the affine path alpha_t = (1-t)alpha + t beta consists of contact forms with the orientation determined by beta \wedge (d beta)^n. We first establish an algebraic criterion: affine deformability is equivalent to the non-negativity of a scalar obtained from the interaction form Theta(alpha, beta) = alpha \wedge (d beta)^n + n beta \wedge d alpha \wedge (d beta)^{n-1}. For unimodular Lie algebras this scalar is (n+1)alpha(Z_beta), where Z_beta is the Reeb vector. We also derive a formula involving the modular character tau(X) = tr(ad_X) in the non-unimodular case. On nilpotent contact Lie algebras, every integrable 1-form is closed; using the standard structural properties of nilpotent contact Lie algebras, this implies that every left-invariant foliation is an affine origin for every fixed contact form. An explicit three-dimensional example illustrates that the modular term can yield affine deformability even when alpha(Z_beta) = 0. We discuss the implications for left-invariant forms on Lie groups and compact quotients. We do not claim a general obstruction example in the non-unimodular case; establishing such an example requires a separate verified construction.

papers.title: Spectral $\Gamma_2$ inequalities for the $V$-Laplacian with evolving weighted measures
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish spectral Bakry-\'{E}mery $\Gamma_2$ criteria and their modified counterparts for the $V$-Laplacian on closed Riemannian manifolds equipped with evolving weighted measures. The estimates yield jointly optimized spectral bounds and sharp endpoint constants. When the measures evolve according to the Fokker-Planck equation, these estimates yield monotonicity formulas for the Fisher information associated with Shannon and Tsallis entropies, together with quantitative propagation of Poincar\'e, logarithmic Sobolev, and nonlinear interpolation inequalities. In the stationary reversible setting, our results specialize to the Witten Laplacian and recover the unweighted Cai-Wang estimates \cite{Cai}.

papers.title: Variations of the harmonic entropy and linear drift on negatively curved surfaces
papers.abstract: For closed negatively curved surfaces, we obtain formulas for the derivatives of the harmonic entropy of its geodesic flow and the linear drift of its Brownian motion along conformal deformations. We deduce that the harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow of a closed surface of non-constant negative curvature (resp. linear drift of the Brownian motion on its universal cover) is strictly decreasing (resp. increasing) along the normalized Ricci flow. We also prove that any hyperbolic metric on a surface admits a neighborhood in the space of conformal negatively curved metrics in which the linear drift is greater or equal to the Liouville entropy, with equality if and only if the metric is hyperbolic.

papers.title: A convexity theorem for proper Dupin hypersurfaces in spheres
papers.abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a (compact, connected, and embedded) proper Dupin hypersurface in a sphere then, viewing $M$ as a submanifold of the ambient Euclidean space, its orthogonal projection to the normal space at any point is convex. This is a generalization of the convexity theorem of Terng for isoparametric submanifolds in Euclidean spaces.

papers.title: $O(3)$-symmetry of four-dimensional steady Ricci solitons
papers.abstract: We prove that a complete connected four-dimensional gradient steady Ricci soliton with positive curvature operator that is $\kappa$-noncollapsed at all scales admits an effective isometric $O(3)$ action preserving the potential function and having principal orbits diffeomorphic to $S^2$.

papers.title: Grassmannian Realizations of Classical Pseudo-Riemannian Symmetric Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a unified fixed-point Grassmannian framework for the classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces from Berger's classification. For a classical group $G=\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(V,b)$, we identify $G$ with the open graph-like locus inside an ordinary or maximal-isotropic Grassmannian $\overline{G}$. Natural involutions of $\overline{G}$ are constructed via classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations. We explicitly describe the full fixed loci of these involutions in terms of classical Grassmannians. The corresponding graph-like fixed loci (or their signature strata) are identified, respectively, with the moduli spaces of classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations; these moduli spaces coincide with classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces. In summary, the 54 classical series are organized into four families: 10 group-type models, 7 classical-form Grassmannians, 20 scalar-structure Grassmannians, and 17 subspace-configuration Grassmannians.

papers.title: Cartan-Ambrose-Hicks theorems and dual geodesic symmetries on statistical manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish Cartan-Ambrose-Hicks (CAH) theorems for statistical manifolds and characterize statistical symmetric spaces by dual geodesic symmetries. These theorems determine statistical structures up to local statisticmorphism by comparing the curvature of an alpha-connection and the skewness tensor using radial geodesics and parallel displacement of that connection. The Levi-Civita formulation characterizes local statisticmorphisms by comparing the radial Jacobi operators of Riemannian curvature and the skewness tensor using Levi-Civita parallel displacement. The same characterization holds with statistical curvature in place of Riemannian curvature. For Hessian manifolds, comparison of the skewness tensor alone is necessary and sufficient. For connected statistical manifolds, we prove the equivalence between the homogeneous definition of statistical symmetric spaces and the existence of global dual geodesic symmetries at every point. The CAH theorems give the necessary and sufficient conditions for maps constructed from exponential maps of dual connections to be local dual geodesic symmetries, preserving the metric and interchanging the dual connections. Such local symmetries exist at every point if and only if the Riemannian curvature and skewness tensors are Levi-Civita parallel. For Hessian manifolds, this condition is equivalent to the equality of the Hessian and dual Hessian curvature tensors.

papers.title: Pontrjagin Classes of Locally Spherically Symmetric Projectively Affine Sprays
papers.abstract: By Chern--Weil theory, rational Pontrjagin classes are represented by curvature forms. Sprays, which require no metric and include all Finsler and Riemannian geodesic sprays, provide a natural setting for the vanishing problem. Shen and Zhao proved that if a manifold admits a locally projectively flat spray, then all of its rational Pontrjagin classes vanish. We ask whether this rigidity persists for the wider class of projectively affine sprays. We prove that if a smooth manifold admits a locally spherically symmetric projectively affine spray, then all rational Pontrjagin classes vanish. Stronger, the Pontrjagin forms of the associated Berwald spray vanish identically as differential forms, a genuine geometric rigidity. Hence a manifold with nonzero rational Pontrjagin class cannot carry such a spray; in particular, it admits no Riemannian metric whose geodesic spray is locally spherically symmetric. We also construct non-Berwald, non-projectively-flat examples with identically vanishing Pontrjagin forms, showing the phenomenon is not a byproduct of projective flatness.

papers.title: Quantitative Rigidity of Ricci Nonnegative Manifolds via the Regular Green Constant
papers.abstract: For a Ricci non-negative non-parabolic manifold $(M^{n\ge3},g)$, assuming the minimal normalized Green function admits the asymptotic expansion $G=r^{2-n}+H_p+O_1(r)$, we prove the scaling invariant defect $H_pR^{n-2}$ controls the geometry of the geodesic ball quantitatively, $\frac{1}{R}d_{GH}(B_p(R),B_0^{\mathbb{R}^n}(R))\le C_n \left(H_p R^{n-2}\right)^{\frac{1}{88(n+1)(4n+1)}}$.
